facts.raw_span: a 4-week history of a rapidly growing left caruncular lesion
an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface, arising from the caruncle
no evidence of PAM (primary acquired melanosis)
The specimen measured 8 × 6 × 5 mm and had a 4-mm ulceration with necrotic tissue on its surface
Revealed a solid tumor with an inflamed crust on its surface, composed of large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity
Showed positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A
The Ki-67 proliferation marker showed a significant number of cycling cells
Sentinel lymph node biopsy findings were negative
Conjunctival and orbital biopsies revealed no tumor
Ulcerated, pedunculated, caruncular tumor
Mitotically active tumor containing anaplastic epithelioid cells
Melanoma cells showing immunoreactivity for Melan-A

concepts.why: The presence of a rapidly growing, ulcerated, pedunculated mass with positive reactivity to melanocytic markers and high mitotic activity supports the diagnosis of malignant melanoma of the caruncle.
The absence of pigmentation and the presence of anaplastic cells with high mitotic activity and positive reactivity to melanocytic markers support the diagnosis of amelanotic melanoma.
The presence of large anaplastic cells with high mitotic activity and positive reactivity to melanocytic markers supports the diagnosis of anaplastic melanoma.
The presence of a melanoma in the caruncle, which is part of the ocular adnexa, supports the diagnosis of melanoma of the ocular adnexa.
The presence of a rapidly growing, ulcerated, pedunculated mass in the caruncle supports the diagnosis of a primary caruncular tumor.
The presence of positive reactivity to melanocytic markers and high mitotic activity supports the diagnosis of a melanocytic tumor.
The presence of a tumor on the ocular surface, specifically in the caruncle, supports the diagnosis of an ocular surface tumor.
The presence of a melanoma in the conjunctiva, which includes the caruncle, supports the diagnosis of conjunctival melanoma.
The Ki-67 proliferation marker showed a significant number of cycling cells, indicating a high-grade tumor.
Sentinel lymph node biopsy findings were negative, suggesting the melanoma is localized and has not spread to the lymph nodes.

rationales.F01: Rapid growth of the lesion suggests a malignant process.
rationales.F02: The presence of an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface is highly suggestive of a malignant melanoma.
rationales.F05: The presence of a solid tumor with an inflamed crust on its surface, composed of large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity, is highly suggestive of a malignant melanoma.
rationales.F06: The positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A confirms the diagnosis of a melanoma.
rationales.F11: The presence of a mitotically active tumor containing anaplastic epithelioid cells is highly suggestive of a malignant melanoma.
rationales.F12: The presence of melanoma cells showing immunoreactivity for Melan-A confirms the diagnosis of a melanoma.
